scope: one local host, existing-init-hook Go overlay, serial cap1,4 child Forks per process;3 alternating control/init pairs; separate warmups; no guest rebuild
conclusion: About17ms lies before server components/plugins; InnoDB plugin about9.3ms, direct buffer-pool-create about1.2ms. The early common path is the next timing target; do not equate all startup time with buffer pool or InnoDB.
recommendation: Continue a bounded split of the early embedded initialization path before claiming a large speed target for #88. Keep #88 as a separate small buffer/RSS hypothesis.
source_findings: pgmem Fresh unpacks base/data directories, optionally creates named DB in standalone PostgreSQL, and forces Go memory return; Fork skips these.
pgmem initial-image COW applies to both paths; it does not alone explain Fresh/Fork difference.
pgmem Fork returns at postmaster readiness before per-client backend startup; prior same-cohort Fork-through-SELECT1 is still9.39ms versus40.03ms for mariamem.
pgmem Close uses discard/kill and deferred memory/segment cleanup; mariamem completes joined runtime/mapping cleanup before lease release. API Close times have different completion boundaries.
limitations: 3 process pairs on one non-isolated host, elapsed substage times with diagnostic overhead; no proven speedup or resource equivalence.
